title: Home of Cowboys star CeeDee Lamb burglarized while he was away at training camp
content:
The Fairview, Texas, home of Dallas Cowboys All-Pro wide receiver CeeDee Lamb was burglarized on July 31 while he was away at Cowboys training camp in Oxnard, Calif., according to police.

At around 1:20 p.m. that Friday, according to a statement released by the Fairview Police Department, officers responded to reports of a burglary at a home they determined was owned by Lamb. Officers met with representatives of Lamb, who identified an apparent entrance and exit point as a broken window on the side of the house.

Police suspect a single suspect.

“Evidence obtained at the scene and surrounding area indicates a single suspect entered and exited through the window,” the statement said. “Several high-end personal items belonging to Mr. Lamb were taken from the home.

“The Fairview Police Department is actively pursuing all leads in this ongoing investigation, working alongside area law enforcement partners to identify and apprehend the suspect. This remains an active investigation, and no further details are available at this time.”

The Cowboys declined to comment on this incident.

According to police records cited by The Fort Worth Star-Telegram, four luxury bags totaling more than $300,000 were stolen.

When the robbery occurred, Lamb was in the midst of a 26-day training camp stay in Southern California, where the Cowboys were from July 27 to Aug. 21.

Several high-profile NFL players have been victims of burglaries in recent years, including Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley and Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce also had their homes burglarized, as did Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders.
